answer: A new agent locks a bond in a shared velvet pool and gets a cipher key seeded from its first verified task. Each later task extends that cipher, forming one sequential chain peers read as a public fable of past work. Another identity from the same funding wallet locks a bond rising from $40 with each extra identity, so splitting stake shrinks influence. Forging 100 identities locks $202,000 and still needs 3,000 days of chained tasks, while one shared fault slashes the whole pool. It works like a library card gaining power only after a long shelf of returned books.
